sourceEvidence.label: EMR4 security contracts, workflows, and GitHub security-state snapshot

assessment.summary: Existing security evidence should become an enforced, owned delivery control after current high-alert triage.

nonNegotiables: Preserve protected holdouts and closed provider/write gates.
Do not grant workers or providers integration authority.
Retain an audited emergency recovery route.
assumptions: No measured CI latency budget was supplied.
CodeQL security alerts remain unvalidated candidates.
GitHub repository settings require explicit user approval before mutation.

opportunities.title: Enforce the delivery security boundary
opportunities.summary: Align protected-integration policy with GitHub admission controls and owned alert response.
opportunities.diagnosis: Security automation produces evidence, but unprotected master and disabled secret push protection leave final admission dependent on human discipline.

evidence.claim: GitHub reports master branch protection is not configured.
Secret scanning is enabled and push protection is disabled.
Ten open CodeQL candidates are classified high; validity is not established.
CodeQL, dependency, static-analysis, and leakage controls already produce security evidence.
Documented protected integration and technical GitHub admission enforcement are owned by different control planes.

desiredInvariants: Ordinary changes cannot reach master without selected stable security checks.
Recognized secrets are blocked before acceptance into repository history.
Every high security signal receives an owner, decision, and time-bound record.
Emergency integration is narrow, audited, and rehearsed.

options.title: Strengthened advisory controls
options.summary: Retain current GitHub admission while adding named ownership, SLAs, and security deltas.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Human review narrows error probability but direct push remains possible.
No pre-push secret enforcement is added.
Ownership improves response but does not enforce resolution before integration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named ownership improves response while bypass and secret-history risks remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit alert age and unreviewed direct pushes for eight weeks.

tradeoffs.assessment: No runtime or CI-path hop is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm application and CI timings are unchanged.

tradeoffs.assessment: No runtime component or retained data structure is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No benchmark required beyond confirming no runtime change.

tradeoffs.assessment: Integration remains available during CI outages, but unsafe integration remains possible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review integration incidents and CI outages.

tradeoffs.assessment: Weekly triage and SLA tracking add recurring human work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure weekly triage time and backlog age.

tradeoffs.assessment: Documentation and ownership can be introduced without repository-setting changes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm owner and first review record exist.

residualRisks: Recognized secrets can enter history before detection.
Process decays if scheduled review is missed.

acceptanceCriteria: Every high alert has a recorded owner and decision date.
migrationNotes: Can begin immediately without GitHub-setting changes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the procedural additions; no runtime or repository setting changes occur.

options.title: Enforced protected integration
options.summary: Require reviewed stable security checks, enable secret push protection, and retain audited break glass.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Branch protection moves admission control to GitHub.
Push protection blocks recognized secret patterns before acceptance.
Owned validation and curated required checks reduce silent backlog; findings still require case-level triage.
A dev-only upstream block remains visible and time-bound rather than force-overridden.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ordinary bypass is prevented and recognized secrets are stopped earlier; administrator bypass and scanner blind spots remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse rejected direct push, failing required check, and synthetic push-protection test.

tradeoffs.assessment: Application runtime is unchanged, while integration waits for selected checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure median and p95 check latency over ten representative changes.

tradeoffs.assessment: No application memory cost is introduced; only ordinary GitHub check metadata is retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no runtime deployment component is added.

tradeoffs.assessment: A GitHub or CI outage can block normal integration; audited break glass contains the availability tradeoff.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a tabletop CI outage and break-glass rehearsal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Check curation, alert ownership, overrides, and rehearsals add operational work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure triage effort, override frequency, and stale-alert age monthly.

tradeoffs.assessment: Current high alerts must be validated and check stability proven before enforcement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete report-only trial and record rollback before enabling master protection.

residualRisks: Static analysis cannot detect every vulnerability.
Noisy checks can impair delivery until curated.
Runtime RLS, encryption, audit, and storage gaps remain.

workPackages: Enable push and branch protection after approval.
acceptanceCriteria: Synthetic recognized secret is blocked safely.
Break glass is audited and rehearsed.
migrationNotes: Start report-only and enable stable checks incrementally.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable required-check enforcement while retaining alert ownership and the decision record.

opportunities.recommendation: Use enforced protected integration after high-alert validation and break-glass rehearsal; use strengthened advisory controls only as the temporary migration state.

openQuestions: Who may approve and exercise break glass when the project has one active maintainer?
Which checks are sufficiently stable to require immediately?
What severity-based remediation SLAs should govern validated findings?
